pr_title: Publish verified Oyatie API contract surface
summary: F4 operator/contributor UX review for PR #1: GitHub metadata shows a 1070-file, 214313-addition bootstrap merged with a failed static ADR-0039 wiring gate and skipped release-attestation lane. Highest severity BLOCKER: operators cannot safely treat this as a verified API baseline until the failed/ skipped verification surfaces are replayed and decomposed.

findings.file: GitHub PR #1 statusCheckRollup: static ADR-0039 wiring gate=FAILURE; release artifact Trivy/Cosign/SBOM lane=SKIPPED
findings.issue: The PR title promises a verified API contract surface, but the operator-visible check rollup says the wiring gate failed and release attestation was skipped. A contributor reading the merged PR has conflicting instructions: trust the baseline or stop on failed verification. That is an ergonomic blocker because the failure mode is policy ambiguity, not an actionable command with a clear next step.
findings.remediation: Replay the ADR-0039/supply-chain and release-attestation lanes against the current baseline SHA, publish the exact pass/fail artifact next to the PR evidence, and mark any still-failing contract group as not verified until fixed.

findings.file: GitHub PR #1 file list: 1070 files, 214313 additions
findings.issue: The initial contract surface landed as a one-piece bootstrap spanning contracts, crates, docs, registries, workflows, and generated metadata. New contributors cannot discover which command owns which contract family or estimate blast radius from the PR surface alone; review ergonomics collapse into repo-wide search.
findings.remediation: Backfill a machine-readable contract inventory grouped by product/domain/contract with owning validation command, rollback path, and baseline evidence SHA so future operators can diff and verify one contract family at a time.
